description:
The document commands stop capping the event log they capture, closing the class `19e7298a` opened.

## Background

`DOCUMENT_CAPTURE_BUDGET` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:5-10`) sets `max_bytes` to 64 MiB with `max_listings: 0`, and the document mutation specs declare `VirtualPath::EVENTS` (`document.rs:295`, `:375`, `:957`). A repository whose event log exceeds 64 MiB therefore cannot link a document, for the same reason `jit claim acquire` could not claim an issue above 16 MiB.

`19e7298a` closed that for the claim and issue-update paths by giving both one `issue_mutation_capture_budget()` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:155`), whose `max_bytes` is unbounded with prose stating why: a capture grows on its own only by expanding a listing, a declared path is not growth (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:586-604`), and the payload that grows is the event log, whose size is the project's own history. `profile.rs`'s `record_capture_budget` (`:2410`) is the older precedent for the same shape.

`commands/config.rs:304` and `commands/init.rs:350` carry hand-picked ceilings too, but declare no event-log path, so neither is exposed to log growth.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A document command succeeds on a repository whose event log exceeds 64 MiB.
- [hard] REQ-02: No capture budget that declares the event log and requests no listings states a byte ceiling the call site cannot derive.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document commands' observable behaviour is otherwise unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test exercises a document command against an event log larger than the previous ceiling and fails if that ceiling returns.

## Notes

Not redo-record work; excluded from the redo-record subtotal of the epic's REQ-06 line balance (`ER-01`). Converge on the existing shape rather than introducing a third form (`@/inv/convention-convergence`).

A budget that requests listings is out of scope. There `max_bytes` is the only bound on real capture growth — a listing expansion names children no declaration mentioned — so removing it deletes a live bound rather than a dead one, and replacing it needs a design for bounding listing expansion. Six such sites declare the event log and keep a ceiling; they are recorded as `SP-04`.
title: Document commands stop capping the event log
